utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure. I may have gone to the brigade command to report on my mission. Do you remember when we talked yesterday, I told you that there was a state of confusion at the reception when I tried to get in touch with Colonel Blagojevic. Do you remember me saying that yesterday? I'm not sure whether I contacted Colonel Blagojevic or Lieutenant Colonel Pajic or maybe the duty operations officer. That is the only reason for why I cannot confirm at this moment whether I got in touch with Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, don't worry about who you might have gotten in touch with. Just did you go back to the brigade to report to someone after Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I cannot answer this question by saying either yes or no. It was a common practice to report on the mission, to debrief the person who gave me the task. But at this moment, I cannot remember whether I was in the command on that day and whether I contacted Colonel Blagojevic or not. That is my problem. I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had brought up the duty officer or Pajic. So did you go back and could you have spoken to one of them after Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Most probably, that was a common practice, but I cannot confirm that I was in the command. I think I may have gone directly to the school, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What do you remember that night after Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I remember driving towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the Kravica warehouse that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of a warehouse in Kravica. Are you referring to military equipment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about any Muslim prisoners being killed at an agricultural co-op warehouse just outside of Kravica, towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. You asked me whether I was in a warehouse, so I thought you referred to military equipment. Of course I'm aware of this agricultural co-op in Kravica, and I heard that some people had been killed there. But on that day I was not in the OKA co-op in Kravica, and the reason why I was not there was that I had been unsuccessful so far. Nobody wanted to talk to me, and I wasn't even aware of the fact that there were people there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew there were people at the Kravica school, but you didn't know there were any people at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And so where did you go in Bratunac when you finally made it back to Bratunac that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I ended up on the second floor of the Vuk Karadzic primary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go back there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I have already answered that question, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't mean to ask you to repeat, but could you just tell us again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Because I had heard and I had seen a vehicle of the military police, and I heard the commander of the military police asking people to help him and his men guarding the huge number of prisoners that they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So when you went back to help secure the prisoners, did you see any shootings that night at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: At the school? You mean inside?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did anybody shoot anywhere at the school or the windows or anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what you saw that was that happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I was on the second floor of the Vuk Karadzic primary school in Bratunac when one of the detainees climbed on the window, started cursing the Chetnik mother, calling people names. I assumed that the Browning started shooting from the Pinzgauer on the windows on the second floor, aiming at the window where this person was standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the bullets or did you know if the bullets hit anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No, nobody was hit. I went downstairs. I tried to explain to this person, whom I had seen standing on the back part of the lorry with his hands on the machine gun. I tried to tell him that if he couldn't -- even if he couldn't care less about the people who were inside, that he could still shoot somebody of our men. He wouldn't talk to me. He just turned his head away from me. I personally tried to reason with this person, although I knew that he was not the most pleasant of people. I decided to -- not to pursue the argument, and I returned to the second floor of the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the same guy you told us about before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's his nickname again? Sorry, I can't pronounce it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Trocijevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And did you stay until the next morning at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did -- what happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the time. When buses appeared, those were the buses that had been parked -- actually, the buses that had been parked set out for Kravica. And after that, new buses started arriving and people on the ground floor were shouting. And somebody said that up to 60 people could get on one bus. And eventually all the people were taken away, were bused away. After that, I went home. I continued my everyday tasks, as before. I apologise. In the morning, I drew the attention to the military policemen to the fact that somebody had broken a window on the second floor in one of the school rooms, and I told them that it is possible that some of the prisoners may have done something to hurt somebody else. So the policemen were standing on one side, and I told them that it would be best for them to stand on one side. All the people left, and finally I left home as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps you could go to, in your book, page 41, line 26. And in the English, page 70, line 3. And I want to ask you a bit about this. Mr. Manning says: "Please continue. It is 1440, explain." And then you say: "It was complete darkness in the school. There were quite a few people who were injured, so you could hear their sounds. These were moans and cries of people who were dying." Did you say that to Mr. Manning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes. There were such people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a true statement, then, what I just read to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: There were people who were screaming. One man repeated throughout the night: Naser, what is the army doing to you? It's a same person who had attacked a guard. On the second floor, there was a man who was also screaming. I believe that he had a gunshot wound on one of his legs. One of his legs was wounded, and that's why I stated that these were the moans and cries of the people who were dying. Maybe this was too strong; however, I would kindly ask you not to adhere to this particular interview, because I cannot at this very moment confirm and remember all those things that I could remember three and a half years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the man who was screaming was shouting: Oh, Naser, what are they doing to your army?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just finish so we can see your whole answer. You go on and say: "We had no way of helping them. I was there. As I told you, it was an incredible situation. I wasn't there in any position of authority. I was there on duty. I didn't come in any function." Are those statements true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes. I had a role as a soldier there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. "My only intention was to go there as a simple soldier and to be there in order to keep some kind of a border. What I mean by this is to also act as some kind of a link and to prevent anything from happening, so as to keep talking, so that we can come to the warning. I had no idea what their intended direction that I'm to go was, whether it was Cazin or Tuzla. I had no idea what was gonna happen to them. And there were different things that Muslims were thinking, but I believe that I had contributed to not creating problems in the sense that I prevented problems from developing." Do you have any problem with any of those things I just read?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Everything is correct. All of that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's break time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could you please inform me how much time do you still need, if less than 15 minutes, so we may continue to finish the direct. But if longer than that, we will break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have a few exhibits to go over with him and a few other readbacks. So it may take a little -- it will take more than 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can just show you a couple of exhibits that you've seen before, I think. The first one is P672. We'll give you the original of this, so you can take a look at it. Do you remember seeing this in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember working with Mr. Manning and making those red marks and numbering them? Do you recall doing that work with Mr. Manning and doing that a long time ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If possible, if we could put the red parts on the ELMO. Witness, if you could take the pointer and just look over at that. Are those -- did you make those red marks describing various locations around Bratunac? Did you do that back with Dean Manning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you -- it's probably easiest just to start with number 1 and just tell us -- go down each of the numbers and tell us briefly what they represent.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The first number is the brigade command, now the overhaul institution. And then also there is the former ceramic tiles factory in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 2 is the military police building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we're talking July of 1995. And number 3, and why don't you point to it just so there's no doubt about what numbers we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you remember what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: That is the monument in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how about number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 4 are the buildings where I survived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's an apartment complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, called Lamele.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 5 is the Vuk Karadzic primary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And number 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 6 is the building for training car mechanics from the secondary school. It's called the hangar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And number 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 7 is the secondary school, which is called Slobodo, ime ti je Tito; Freedom, your name is Tito.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Number 8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I think that number 8 is the SUP building, the SUP building. I'm not sure. I think that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the last one I think is number 9.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Number 9, number 9 I think is the bus station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you remember where you saw buses and trucks lined up on that afternoon evening of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe, using this map, roughly where you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's on the road in front of number 9?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: In front of the bus station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: On this road here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the long road between the bus station and number 5, the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: That road is about 400 metres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The buses were here, on this road and on this road here, towards the monument, here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you indicate "here towards the monument," you're --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Indicating it's sort of under number 3 moving in the direction towards number 5 along a road. And when you said buses were in front of the Vuk Karadzic school, could you point out that road again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I did not say the buses were in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. That would have been here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thought you just pointed to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Buses were here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: In this street, and I think the two or parked here in this area over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said "here in this area," you mean near the monument?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you're saying that their buses were parked on this road that comes out perpendicular towards the Vuk Karadzic school and goes towards the bus station, sort of between number 5 and number 9. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And let me show you another exhibit. This is 671, but don't put it on the ELMO because it's got your name on it. Just take a look at it. And if you could just hand that to the witness, if you could. And we should have colour maps for Your Honours. I saw a black and white one-up there, but let me just give you that one. Can you tell us what this map is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: This map is the working map of the chief of engineers of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this an actual copy of an actual map that you were using at the time, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's got a date on it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So was this in use after the fall of Srebrenica? I think it's November, if I remember right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just briefly tell us what this map shows.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The areas of responsibility of the respective battalions. What can also be seen marked in light red are the mines and other explosives that have not been removed, and the green areas are those that were removed. And the dark red denotes the possible mines that could be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's all I wanted to ask you about. Now, do you remember telling Mr. Manning that one of the, I believe, it was pioneers was killed by a mine, one of your pioneers was killed by a mine near the time of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you told us at that time that you remembered his first name was Dragan. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were we able to show you any document that helped you remember his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now do you remember his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The late Dragan Andric. May he rest in peace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just show you the page that we had shown you. It's Exhibit Number 673.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, you have seen July 14th of the health record of Bratunac. This is that same record, but we did not put in the 12th. So this is from the 12th of July. The other exhibit that Mr. Butler talked about was 474 -- 464, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what part of this document -- can you put this on the ELMO and can you just tell us what part of this document helped you remember this person's name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you recognise that as the person that was killed on that day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on that same subject, do you remember me showing you what is exhibit 159. It was a report that talked about 12 July, and you may recall it talked about Mico Gavric heading some deminers. And one of the Sappers being killed. Do you remember that? Do you remember reading that document? I can get you a copy so you can see it again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The reference in that report regarding the Sapper being killed, it didn't name the person. But is the information in that report consistent with Mr. Andric being killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I don't know, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything in that information that you didn't think was right, and I can let you see that document so you can just take a look at it, like the location you remember you were telling us about, the location of where you thought he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps it would be a good idea if I had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the B/C/S version is 159/A. And if we can just put the English version on the ELMO so everybody can see it. And what I wanted to ask you about just to help us clarify a little bit about this document, if you can, had you ever seen this document before, as far as you know, before I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No, I do not remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the part I want you to look at is it says: "Between 0500 and 0630 hours, the pioneers of the Bratunac Brigade led by Captain Gavric cleared passage through a minefield or groups of mines towards Budok [phoen] or immediately around Zuti Most/Potocari road. Members of the 1st Company of the Zvornik special police unit led by a pioneer from the Bratunac Brigade set off through the cleared passages toward Potocari to create the conditions of the introduction of hardware. As personnel were being introduced, a Sapper stepped on a prong. He was taken to the Bratunac health centre where he died and in a way this incident slowed down the advance." Does any of the information I just read sound familiar to you? Do you know anything about Mico Gavric in this operation, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No. My information about this was that I came with the late Dragan to the place where he was supposed to open the minefield, but that locality was not mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I told you before that I did not have that much influence over these people and that I did not have enough time to centralise the entire demining team, hence the difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. One other document I wanted to show you, it's 406/B in the B/C/S version. 406/A, the 5 July order for active combat under the name of Commander Blagojevic. Do you remember if you had seen this document prior to me showing it to you in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Did I see this document before you showed it to me in your office you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember at the time anyone showing that to you or you being able to read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We have one other exhibit I wanted to show to you, that is Exhibit 674. Do you remember seeing this piece of a map in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you point with the pointer -- are you able to see here on this map of Kravica where the Kravica school is that you visited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I think I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have the little pointer there. You can mark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it -- there's some bigger buildings there with an SK next to it. Does that mean skola, school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes. I think it means skola, school, in that sense. The letter S and then K.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the school is that you went to see that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I was at the school during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, during the day. Is that the same school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I think that's the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you know anything about any reburial of any bodies in Bratunac to some other location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember telling Dean Manning that everybody knew about the operation or that you could smell it? That's what I mean. That's the thing that I'm talking about. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you remember about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I remember that I was sitting at home. The window was open, my room window, and I felt this incredible stench. I know what the stench of decaying human bodies is. The following day I heard stories that children in the street saw some legs, parts of human bodies. That's all I know about this. This may mean that some graves were being relocated or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about what did this, who relocated the graves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work with Mr. Dragan Jokic before the fall of Srebrenica or after on any work matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: After the fall of Srebrenica, I worked with Major Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what capacity? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I was the officer responsible for demining the area of Bratunac, the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what kind of work did you do with Mr. Jokic from the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I handed over all reports to Mr. Jokic, and the records compiled by myself or others in respect of minefields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what position was Mr. Jokic to you? Was he any kind of superior or someone you looked up to in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic was not my superior, but -- I mean, he was not my official superior, but he was a man who was appointed by the corps to centralise information and to submit this information to IFOR or the corps, I don't know. At any rate, he asked me to provide all information to him about demining and also information that we had in respect of existing minefields.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever able to get any Muslim information about minefields?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Not from Muslims, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes. People were coming in. My deminers found notebooks they found in the area with some records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those Muslim -- were those Muslim notebooks engineering-type records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that is precisely what I was collecting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you pass those on to Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: To Mr. Jokic or to the commander of the 55th Engineering Regiment from Konjevic Polje, at that time Major Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find Mr. Jokic? Was he helpful and professional?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Towards what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards you, towards his job. Just what can you tell us about his character?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic often did not have any understanding for possible improvements in our work or suggestions made to that effect. We often entered debates of this nature. On one occasion in the Zvornik Brigade in his office, Mr. Jokic, perhaps provoked by my question, when I received orders from the corps to provide all information to the Zvornik Brigade so that they would be centralised - and this should also have been provided to IFOR in Tuzla, the database there - at that time, Mr. Jokic asked me to hand over all the papers to him. I had an order in my hands from the corps command, and I said to him: I'm sorry, sir, but I don't know you, in respect of this document. He was very nervous and he did not have any understanding, as far as I was concerned. Ultimately I did hand over all these papers to him. I would not like to draw any conclusions. I do not consider myself to be an educated person, and I could therefore not judge an officer of higher rank than my own. I have mentioned the specific situation to you, and you can draw your own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you tell us that you thought Jokic was someone you looked up to as a professional engineer? Didn't you tell us that? That's why I asked the question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No, I didn't tell you that. I told you that about Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about Colonel Blagojevic, his character, what you think about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I can give you an example, but I don't deem myself fit to judge an officer who was my superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I mean a good example? What do you mean by "example"? Well, if you don't want to talk about that, I won't ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't think I have any further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I do have a little bit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I could borrow the podium from Prosecution, I would most appreciate it. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me start with your background. As I understand it, you said earlier that you went to a military secondary school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, when you were interviewed by the Prosecution back on 29 November, 2001, you had indicated that you left the school, that military secondary school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you told us that that school that had originally -- that was originally located in Sarajevo had then been transferred to another location. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's not quite accurate that you left. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me be very blunt. Isn't it a fact that you were thrown out of that school, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: That true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were thrown out because you had taken a truck, I believe it's a TAM 110. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have a driver's license at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't have permission to drive that truck either, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a permission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took it nonetheless and you went swimming. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you were thrown out of school, and that's how you ended up back in Bratunac to finish up at that trade school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, you went to the academy, which I believe is in Banja Luka. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a one-year programme?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, you were there to become an engineer of sorts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked a question about whether as a student you had gone to the frontline. Do you remember being asked that question by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the places you mentioned that you had gone to was Bihac, to the frontline. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after about seven days, you escaped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I thought I would get that reaction. After about seven days of being there, you left your post without authorisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: That is not true, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's not true that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maybe we can go into a -- into -- is it private session? Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you left, you were still a lieutenant, were you not? That was my point, that you were a lieutenant in 1995 and you were still a lieutenant back in 2002 - that's the point that I'm trying to - make when you voluntarily left?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the references to "me" and "I" and "I feel," this personalising everything, which brings it to a level that it doesn't need to go. So I would object to the personalisation. The same thing can be said without injecting his own personage each time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again, I have an objection to the cross-examination. Another untruth was told. I didn't leave the army as a lieutenant; I left as a captain. What is this man here trying to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, just tell us the truth. I think that you are here to help us, not to help the Defence counsel. I think the Defence counsel has some questions which may be to the credibility. And if you have some problems, just let us know, as you did now. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you met with the Prosecutor over there. Could you tell us for how long. For how long did you -- y'all talk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I arrived in the building of the Tribunal at 11.00, but I'm not sure, and I left the building - again I'm not sure - but I think so it was 4.00 or half past 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as I understand it, you offered to read your statement, but you chose to read it after you and the Prosecutor had your conversations. Is that correct? From the notes that I have, they gave you an opportunity to read your statement, but you elected to read it later, not at the beginning, prior to the questioning process or the proofing process with the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No. I didn't read my statement before the conversation with the Prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was because you chose not to? That was your choice, not that they didn't give you the opportunity or the time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I didn't ask to do it. I didn't know that I was entitled to do it. The Prosecutor gave me the statement when I could not remember everything that I had stated. So I did not read my statement before my conversation with the Prosecutor, if that is your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, he did show you some other documents. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ask to see other documents to help your memory, or was he showing you documents trying to prompt your memory into seeing if you could recall something by what others might have said, what might be contained in other documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The Prosecutor gave me all the documents in order to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a problem with your memory, that it needed refreshing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I still have problems. I can't remember what happened eight and a half years ago. I can't remember exactly where I was at what time on what dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was your memory back on 29 November, 2001, when you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: No. Again, it wasn't really very good. Sir, if you have been listening to me, I had said on three or four occasions that I am confused about some of the events. I have told you everything that I can remember, and as far as my statement is concerned, I gave the statement to the gentleman in Banja Luka, but I didn't mention any specific times or dates. I just covered a certain period of three or four days, and I told him that I couldn't remember whether I had gotten in touch with Colonel Blagojevic at a certain time. I cannot remember, and I adhere to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the gentleman that you spoke to yesterday was also in the room part of the time back on November 29, 2001, when you were giving your statement. And I'm wondering: Was he giving you any documents back then to try to refresh your memory to see if you could recollect anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The first meeting?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Would you give me a moment, please. Documents were shown to me, but not to refresh my memory. It's not that I can say that. Those were the documents that were shown here today, the document with the map, the map of the chief of engineers of the brigade, and the map where I circled the numbers from 1 to 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday when you were being -- when you were having your memory refreshed, did he show you any statements, say, from Mr. Petrovic, the person that had been injured, to see whether he could -- whether you could take a look at what he might have said as far as what he was doing and the date when he was injured, to see if that would refresh your memory. Did he do that by any chance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The Prosecutor did not show me Mr. Petrovic's statement, but I was shown a piece of paper. I don't know whether I have the right -- I mean, I cannot remember this document exactly, but somebody's report was contained in it, that Sreten Petrovic had been wounded in action. That document was shown to me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: So that I could orient myself in terms of when various events took place, because I really have a problem in terms of connecting those three days when things happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he show you any reports by their own military analysts, for instance, that would show that there's no evidence that anybody was in the Kravica school on the day that you have indicated that you went and visited? This would have been, I believe, the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. I know that is a misstatement of the evidence. I don't know what he's referring to. And if now the Prosecution is personally on trial through this witness, I don't understand the relevance. Our proofing notes provided the documents that this man has seen to the best of our recollection, and I can agree with Mr. Karnavas, those are the only documents that was shown to him. If he wishes to make this argument that he brought up earlier, that's fine. It's his right. But to -- trying to use the witness is -- I don't see how that's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it seems to me that you are engaging in a fishing expedition, and I'm not questioning about your question, but if you ask this question you better lay some foundations on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One last question about the proofing. I don't want to go into it too much, but I couldn't help when going through your 86-page statement, I never see the name of Major Jokic in here. You never once mention him. So my question is: What prompted you yesterday to have this exchange with the Prosecutor about Mr. Jokic? Did you volunteer it or were they on a fishing expedition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: This is how Mr. Jokic was discussed yesterday during the conversation. We were talking about what I was actually looking for in the schools and the places where prisoners of war were. I explained to the gentleman that my mission was to try to find the records of minefields of the Muslim side. You probably heard that. As we continued talking, the gentleman asked me: Why were you doing that? Why were you collecting this information? Because I was the officer who was in charge of demining in the Bratunac Brigade, by the Bratunac Brigade, with IFOR. Why was I in contact with Major Jokic? That's when I mentioned his name. That's when the Prosecutor asked me: What kind of contact did you have with Major Jokic? And then I explained it to him and I told him the truth. I did not have any contact with Major Jokic before Srebrenica or did I know Major Jokic before Srebrenica. Our first contact was when SFOR or IFOR asked for the centralisation of documents for demining to be sent to be processed at the centre in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now you have your statement in front of you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, I have noticed you take it with you, and I assume that you brought it with you today, correct, your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that at some point after meeting with the Prosecutor there, you sat and you read your statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: During the meeting, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, afterwards. Yesterday afternoon, last night, this morning, you've read it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes. I really made an effort to read it, sir -- not to read it, but to see what I stated so that I wouldn't take up these people's time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Exactly. And it just so happens that on page 1 - it would be page 2 of the English version - and I'm quoting now from -- I have a draft transcript, this would be introduced as D91/1. (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be the very first page. On the English version, it's line -- it's page 2, line 9 and 10. On your version, is it towards the bottom of the page, about four or five sentences above the bottom of the page on page 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, I see that now. It is line 48.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that when you read it? Did you see it when you were reading your statement. Did you notice that you had stated to the folks in Banja Luka that you had the post of chief of engineers of the Bratunac Brigade? Did you see that when you were reading your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yesterday, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, if we were to go through this statement, we would

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me get this straight. You don't know whether you were appointed or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think this question is quite clear, and we understand your point. It's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To finish this section?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a section, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you what has been marked as D90/1 for identification purposes. Did the Prosecutor show you this document to refresh your memory yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We're at a little bit of a disadvantage --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't have the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: I probably had to see it. It is addressed to me, and I must have seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What's the date, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: The 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And this is your -- this is an order, in a sense, appointing you, correct, to your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there more than one platoon of engineers in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: How do you see this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you. You have three squads, right, in the third ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-135
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. In every battalion, there was one platoon respectively consisting of ten men, so that is, in fact, one platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, we can break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I have to remind you that this witness is under the protective measures. So the document you used just now should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And since you are going to bring up this question for the future days, I hope you could remind this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll try to remember, Your Honour -- I will remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another two days. And please do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony, because you are under the oath. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood you loud and clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And tomorrow we'll resume at 2.15 in the same courtroom, that is in Courtroom I instead of Courtroom III. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
